passage:
I'm Charu, Rekha's roommate, and I saw the change before Rekha said a word.

In the canteen on Tuesday the usual group was joking about Sameer's old laptop with its cracked corner, and how he "must be selling it soon". Rekha laughed loudly, the way you laugh to belong.

Two days later, at the placement workshop, someone joked about the borrowed blazer Rekha wore, sleeves too long. Rekha smiled, then went to the washroom and stayed a while. That evening Rekha said, to nobody in particular, "Being the joke is awful."

On Friday, when the group started on Sameer again, Rekha said, "I'll pass, that's getting old," and picked up a tray. Nobody answered. I can't say what Rekha felt, but Rekha then walked over to Sameer's table and asked about the laptop stickers.

qa.q: What did the group joke about Sameer?
qa.a: His old laptop with its cracked corner, and that he "must be selling it soon".

qa.q: How did Rekha seem to feel after the joke about the borrowed blazer, and what is uncertain?
qa.a: Hurt, judging by the smile followed by a long stay in the washroom and the remark "Being the joke is awful". Charu cannot be sure of Rekha's inner state.

qa.q: What did Rekha do that a wise friend might do?
qa.a: Rekha quietly refused to join in with "I'll pass, that's getting old" and then reached out to Sameer.

qa.q: How might Sameer have felt about the jokes and Rekha's later question?
qa.a: Probably stung by the canteen jokes, and a friendly question about the stickers may feel like being seen as more than the joke.

grounding: Rekha laughs along at Sameer's expense to fit in, feels what it is like to be the joke, and quietly refuses, seen by a roommate.

passage:
Late on Sunday, in the class group chat:
Pallavi: guys look at Somesh's presentation photo
Pallavi: who wears a tie to a class presentation
Kunal: looks like a bank manager
Jatin: hahaha
Then, a few minutes later:
Jatin: ok wait. i laughed but honestly
Jatin: last year you all roasted my hometown accent for a month and i hated it
Jatin: somesh probably dressed up because he was nervous
Pallavi: it's just banter jatin
Jatin: maybe. doesn't feel like banter when you're the one in the photo
Jatin: i'm deleting my haha
Pallavi: ok fine. deleting the pic too
Kunal: 👍
Jatin: thanks. see you all in class tomorrow
Pallavi: yeah. and i'll tell somesh the tie looked sharp, actually 🙂

qa.q: What did Pallavi share in the group chat?
Why did Jatin change course after typing "hahaha"?
qa.a: Jatin remembered being roasted for a hometown accent and hating it, and felt uneasy and guilty about laughing at Somesh.

qa.q: Which choice worked for Jatin, and why?
qa.a: Saying it plainly without attacking anyone and deleting the "haha"; it made it easy for Pallavi to delete the photo too.

qa.q: How might Somesh feel if he saw the chat?
qa.a: Humiliated and hurt, since he probably dressed up because he was nervous.

grounding: Shows laughing along at someone's expense to fit in, then recalling being on the other side and quietly refusing to call it banter.

passage:
On the college bus from the villages outside Kottayam, the back seats had a game: whenever Chandrika from the dairy family got on, someone would hold their nose and moo softly. Jomon always laughed. It was easier than being the one who didn't.
On Monday Chandrika got on with her hands tucked into her dupatta, and Binu started the moo. Jomon's laugh came out, then stuck halfway. He remembered his own first week, when the same boys called him "rubber-tapper's son" until he stopped wearing his father's old shirt.
He didn't make a speech. When Binu nudged him to moo too, he said, "Nah, leave it," and moved to the empty seat two rows ahead, near Chandrika. He asked if the chemistry practical was still on Thursday.
She glanced at him warily. "Yes. Thursday."
Behind them, the mooing trailed off. Binu called him boring. Jomon looked out at the rubber trees and let him.

qa.q: What did the back seats do whenever Chandrika got on?
qa.a: Held their noses and mooed softly.

qa.q: Why did Jomon's laugh stick halfway on Monday?
qa.a: He remembered being called "rubber-tapper's son" and felt uncomfortable and ashamed, recognising how it feels on the other side.

qa.q: How did Jomon quietly refuse to join in?
qa.a: He said "Nah, leave it", moved to the seat near Chandrika and talked to her normally about the practical.

qa.q: How might Chandrika see Jomon sitting near her?
qa.a: Warily at first, unsure whether it's another trick, but possibly relieved when the mooing trails off.

grounding: Illustrates laughing along at someone's expense, noticing how it feels from the other side, and quietly refusing to continue.
